liebermann.description_de: Paris, Bibl. nation., Lat. 4771, früher Colbert 3860
liebermann.shelfmark_as_given: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Lat. 4771, formerly Colbert 3860
liebermann.laws: Cons Cn, In Cn, I Cn, II Cn, Af, II Eg, Ine, Mirce, Að, Had, Grið, Geþyncðo, Hu, Wl art, ECf retr
liebermann.notes: Perhaps written and glossed in Kent, in France since the 15th century; contains the prologue of Consiliatio Cnuti, Instituta Cnuti with parts of Af, II Eg and Af–Ine, Mirce, Að, Had, Grið, Geþyncðo, Hu, then the Tripartita (Wl art, ECf retr, Genealogia Normannica continued to 1170 and 1189). Cb was copied in Ko.

others.text: O’Brien (2003): dated c. 1175 rather than c. 1160. Cb is the work of a reviser: it grafts the prologue and some chapters of the Consiliatio Cnuti onto the full text, and has many readings of its own (fines spelled out in pounds and shillings, the number of oath-helpers made exact, a long added gloss at I 5,2). It shows how Cnut’s law was understood c. 1175 but is of very limited use for recovering the original text. O’Brien traces much of the trouble with Liebermann’s text to the high place he gave Cb.
